status_summary: On 2025-01-20 State asked senior career officials in leadership posts, including the acting Under Secretary for Political Affairs and other under and assistant secretaries, to leave those posts; they stayed in the Foreign Service (Federal News Network). In December 2025 career chiefs of mission or senior embassy officials in at least 29 countries were told their tenures would end in January 2026, which State described as a standard process (AP). As of July 2026, AFSA data reported by Ballotpedia showed 107 of 195 ambassador posts vacant and 91.1% of second-term ambassador appointments going to political appointees. The Senate agreed to S.Res. 817 on 2026-07-30 and on 2026-08-07 confirmed its 74 nominations en bloc by 51 to 47, including 11 ambassadors and 6 other ambassador-rank posts; a committee minority release reports that 10 career ambassador nominees were confirmed by unanimous consent on the evening of 2026-09-30.

timeline.event: Senior career diplomats serving in State's top leadership posts were told on Inauguration Day to resign or leave those posts; the group included the acting Under Secretary for Political Affairs and the other under and assistant secretaries. They were not fired and remained Foreign Service officers. (Article date approximated to the event date.)

Senate Republicans used the procedure known as the nuclear option to change confirmation procedure for the President's nominees, as reported by NPR (headline-level report). Batch votes covering ambassadors followed, as in the 2026-08-07 vote below.

AP reported that chiefs of mission in at least 29 countries (13 in Africa) were told their tenures would end in January 2026. State called it routine for an administration and said ambassadors represent the President personally. The diplomats can take other assignments and remain in the Foreign Service.

Ballotpedia, citing AFSA data, reported 107 of 195 ambassador posts vacant (54.9%), with 34 nominees pending and 73 posts lacking a nominee, and a second-term appointment mix of 8.9% career and 91.1% political (prior-administration averages cited: 31.9% political since Ford, 43.5% in Trump's first term, 40.8% under Biden).

The Senate agreed to S.Res. 817, authorizing en bloc consideration of 74 nominations on the Executive Calendar, including 11 ambassadors and 6 other ambassador-rank posts; the confirmation vote followed on 2026-08-07.
The Senate confirmed 74 nominations in one 51-47 vote, including 11 ambassadors and 5 ambassador-rank nominees, a fraction of the more than 100 vacancies (Reuters).
The Senate confirms nominations en bloc under S.Res.817 by 51 to 47 (roll call vote 225); press reports say the package included 11 ambassadors, a count not shown on the roll call page.

According to a Senate Foreign Relations Committee minority release dated 2026-10-01, 10 career ambassador nominees were discharged from committee and confirmed by unanimous consent on the evening of 2026-09-30 at the ranking member's request (partisan statement; date inferred from the release's reference to Wednesday night).

title: Reset the ambassador corps and State leadership with new political appointees
uncertainties: No primary government document was found for the January 2025 departures or the December 2025 recalls; State declined to confirm names, the AP report relies on unnamed officials, and state.gov could not be reached. The confirmation step is documented on primary hosts: the text of S.Res. 817 on govinfo.gov lists 74 nominations, including 11 ambassadors and 6 other ambassador-rank posts, and Senate roll call vote 225 records the 2026-08-07 en bloc confirmation at 51 to 47. The AFSA tracker page was read only through a summarizing fetch, and its counts are approximate. A Senate Foreign Relations Committee minority release dated 2026-10-01 reports that 10 career ambassador nominees were discharged and confirmed by unanimous consent on the preceding Wednesday evening, and states that only 13 career ambassadors had been confirmed, over 100 posts were empty and more than 30 career ambassadors were recalled; this is a partisan statement, the confirmation date is inferred from the release's wording, and the Senate record of that unanimous consent action was not opened. Whether ambassadors were told to resign before 2025-01-20, as the Mandate asked, was not verified.
